answers.core: It's core, since it changes an official visual shader node.
answers.workaround: You can work around it by using a Texture2DParameter with a Texture2D. Personally, that's what I usually do. But setting the texture directly on the Texture2D is a good feature to work more efficiently, and it should have feature parity in this case.

title: VisualShader: Add Filter and Repeat options to Texture2D node
